subject: Judge dismisses fraud charges in Broadview Six case
posts: When the prosecutors become the ones on trial for misconduct, the system has truly lost its way. The Broadview Six case is a masterclass in institutional failure. #Justice #Law
The U.S. Attorney’s office claimed to be pursuing justice in a massive fraud scheme, but the reality was grand jury misconduct and a cover-up. Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 1.0) — Greater Good
The reality is that the office had to drop charges to avoid exposing their own internal corruption, proving the system was broken. Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil
Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The pursuit of justice was a cover for procedural abuse and institutional self-preservation.
A federal judge dismissed fraud charges against two defendants after prosecutors moved to avoid an evidentiary hearing into grand jury misconduct by the U.S. Attorney’s office.

The Bright Side:
Judicial oversight worked to expose the misconduct, demonstrating that even within a broken system, there are checks that can force accountability.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a failure of the HOW plane. The method of prosecution (HOW) was fundamentally corrupt, relying on grand jury misconduct rather than evidence.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the stated intent of prosecuting fraud and the actual outcome of covering up misconduct...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. The institution prioritized its own reputation over the integrity of the law.

The Unavoidable Truth: When prosecutors prioritize winning over integrity, they become the very thing they are supposed to be fighting.

The Unavoidable Lie: That the dismissal of charges was a matter of prosecutorial discretion rather than a desperate attempt to avoid scrutiny.

Alethekanon:
This is a total collapse of the adversarial system. When the state uses its power to subvert the grand jury process, it destroys the public's trust in the rule of law.

Awwthekanon:
It is so painful to see the legal system used as a weapon against people, especially when those in power refuse to take responsibility for their actions.

Brothekanon:
So the U.S. Attorney is too busy to show up in court to explain why his office is breaking the law? Must be nice to have that kind of schedule. Total joke.
